Looking at each chapter carefully, I'll test sentences against the six structural failure criteria, excluding anything that is a direct residue of authorized cuts.

---

**Ch 022 draft, mid-scene jump candidate:**

The draft opens Chapter 22 with Adams's boyhood visit to Harvard, then moves through the Cambridge years, then pivots to the Western trip:

> "When the first year of professing and editing was at last over, he took the next train for the West."

The source bridges this with: "Putting in his pocket the July number of the North American, with a notice of the Fortieth Parallel Survey by Professor J. D. Whitney, he started for the plains and the Rocky Mountains." — and crucially, earlier in the chapter, the source introduces Frank Emmons explicitly: "One of his friends from earliest childhood, and nearest neighbor in Quincy, Frank Emmons, had become a geologist and joined the Fortieth Parallel Survey under Government. At Washington in the winter of 1869-70, Emmons had invited Adams to go out with him." The draft omits this entirely, then uses Emmons's name as a given:

> "Emmons's party was out of reach in the Uintahs, but Arnold Hague's had come in to Laramie for supplies, and they took charge of Adams for a time."

The draft has not introduced Emmons anywhere. A reader with no source access encounters "Emmons's party" with no established referent — Emmons has never been named in the draft.

**Gate test**: A competent reader would be genuinely confused — "Emmons" is a proper name with no antecedent anywhere in the draft, not a generic descriptor that can be inferred. The reader cannot tell who Emmons is or why his party's location matters.

Note: The authorized subplot removal is "Western geological field-trip with the Fortieth Parallel Survey (Ch 021)." But this is Ch 022, and the Emmons introduction occurs in Ch 022 source material that was *not* marked for removal — the drafter preserved the Estes Park scene and Clarence King meeting but silently dropped the Emmons introduction that precedes them. This is not a residue of an authorized cut.
